Turn interface motion on or off — Off feels snappier on older phones and tablets
Use HDR output when the video & screen support it. mpv only: the ExoPlayer engine does not support this setting and always passes the stream’s HDR through.
Match the screen\'s refresh rate to the video (24/25/50/60 fps) in full screen, for Live TV and VOD, and restore it on exit. Turn off if the screen flickers or goes dark when a video starts.

This device runs Android %1$s. Below Android 12 the device can\'t tell OwnTV which refresh rates it can switch to smoothly, so changing the rate may black the screen out for a second or two — sometimes more than once during a programme.\n\nWe recommend leaving Auto frame rate off here. If your screen switches cleanly, turn it on and see: you can change it back at any time.

Decode Dolby/DTS to surround (5.1/7.1) for a real 5.1/7.1 receiver connected to this device. Leave OFF for the built-in speaker, headphones or a stereo soundbar — multichannel can lag audio behind video. If it drifts, nudge the player\'s Audio menu → A/V sync.

On: Dolby and DTS go undecoded to the TV, soundbar or receiver when it says it can play them (ExoPlayer). Off: the app decodes them, still as surround where Surround sound allows. mpv always decodes. Not used while Night mode or Volume leveling is on.

On: Dolby and DTS go undecoded to a connected TV or receiver when it says it can play them (ExoPlayer). Off: the app decodes them, still as surround where Surround sound allows. mpv always decodes. Not used while Night mode or Volume leveling is on.
Turns loud scenes down and quiet dialogue up, for watching at a low volume.
Brings every channel and movie slowly to the same loudness, so switching does not jump in volume.
The highest picture played when a channel or movie offers several. Saves bandwidth and eases the decoder.
On a metered connection, plays at most this quality. Off: the same as on Wi-Fi.

Live TV on ExoPlayer: the TV\'s own hardware keeps picture and sound together, with less work for the processor. Works on some TVs only, and turns itself off if a channel fails with it. Audio sync cannot be nudged while it is on.

Live TV on ExoPlayer: the device\'s own hardware keeps picture and sound together, with less work for the processor. Works on some devices only, and turns itself off if a channel fails with it. Audio sync cannot be nudged while it is on.

Use the device\'s hardware decoder. Turn off if some streams stutter or show artifacts.

How far ahead films, episodes and catch-up are loaded. Auto uses what suits this device. A longer buffer rides out a bad connection better; this device’s memory still sets the limit, so a high-bitrate film may hold less than chosen.
How long films, episodes and catch-up wait on a silent server before the connection counts as lost. Auto keeps each player’s own wait: 60 seconds on mpv, 20 on ExoPlayer.
How many times a film or episode that loses its connection is reopened where it stopped before an error is shown. A minute of steady playback earns the attempts back.
Plays this audio track when the stream has it. \"Original language\" plays films and series in the language they were made in.
Show your provider\'s channel number beside the name in the Live TV list and the player. Off hides every number; nothing is lost, and turning it back on restores them.
Left and right rewind live TV
With the controls hidden, Left and Right rewind and go forward on channels you can rewind (catch-up, or saved by Pause and rewind live TV), instead of opening the channel list and history.
Channels without catch-up are saved on this device while you watch them full screen, so you can pause and rewind. Writes to storage all the time; at least 1 GB always stays free.
How far back you can rewind a channel without catch-up.
What happens when you come back to a channel that was saved while you were away.

Show live fps, bitrate and dropped frames in the stream-info overlay (measured while the overlay is open, for streams that don\'t declare these values). Turn off only if a low-end device stutters — it never affects the actual video, only the diagnostic numbers.

mpv (recommended) has the widest format support — DTS/TrueHD audio, unusual files. ExoPlayer plays some streams mpv can\'t on certain devices, but can\'t decode DTS/TrueHD audio. The combined options try the other player automatically when the first one fails; the single-player options never do, which saves a few seconds of black screen if the second player never works on your device.

ExoPlayer (recommended) opens channels much faster and is the only one with live subtitles. mpv plays channels ExoPlayer can\'t, including some with unusual audio. The combined options try the other player automatically when the first one fails; the single-player options never do, which saves a few seconds of black screen if the second player never works on your device. A channel you switch by hand in the player keeps your choice either way.
Reset saved live TV player choices

Switching a channel between ExoPlayer and mpv in the player saves that choice for the channel. Reset makes every channel follow the “Live TV player” setting again. Saved choices for movies and episodes are kept.
Reset saved live TV player choices?
Every channel goes back to the “Live TV player” setting. You can always switch an individual one again from the player.

The player learns what each provider’s streams need — mpv instead of ExoPlayer, another format, software decoding for catch-up. Forget this if a provider has fixed its streams. Catch-up lessons are also forgotten on their own after 14 days.
Channels open the standard way again, and the player relearns whatever a provider still needs. The first play of an affected channel may take a few seconds longer.

%1$d%% zoom shows many more items on screen at once. On devices with limited memory this can make the app unstable or crash, especially with large playlists and EPG data.\n\nChoose Cancel to stay at %2$d%%.
Hold OK on Move, Rename or Hide for the first item, then press the same on the last. Everything in between changes together.
CH+ / CH− skip a page. Hold CH+ / CH− to jump to the last or first item.

Auto — try Dolby/DTS surround, and switch back to stereo automatically if the speaker, headphones or connected receiver do not play it. Recommended.
Stereo only — always decode in the app and send plain 2.0 sound. Use this for the built-in speaker, headphones or a stereo soundbar, or if audio lags behind the picture.

Each viewer keeps their own favorites, watch history, resume points and Home rows. Kids mode shows only the categories you allow; a PIN stops anyone else from opening the profile.
Add a playlist from a link, an Xtream login, a Stalker portal or a file, re-sync one, or remove it.
Add an XMLTV guide feed by its link, refresh it, or remove it. Feeds fill the TV Guide and the program lines in Live TV.
How many days of programs the guide stores ahead. Fewer days make guide refreshes faster and the database smaller.

Catch-up plays programs from your provider’s archive. Most providers run it on your TV’s own clock; choose a fixed UTC offset if catch-up starts at the wrong time. This is also where you choose which player catch-up uses.
Dark is what OwnTV is designed for. System follows the TV’s own setting where it has one; Light suits a bright room.
Tints buttons, the focus glow, progress bars and highlights everywhere. Pick a preset, or press OK for the palette and any hex code.
The ring drawn around whatever has focus. Pick its color and thickness so it stays easy to follow from the sofa.
The font used across OwnTV, and how large text is drawn. Popups use the same font.
Makes popups, menus and dialogs larger or smaller as a whole. Use it when popups feel cramped or cover too much of the screen.
Scales everything on screen. Larger is easier to read from a distance; smaller fits more on screen. Below 85%% low-memory TV boxes can run out of memory.
Sheets, menus and focus move smoothly while this is on. Off makes every change instant.
Shows the temperature and your town next to the clock. Set a location by hand when the automatic one is wrong — behind a VPN, for example — and choose Celsius or Fahrenheit.

Floating: the menu rests as a small capsule over the content and slides open when you move left. Docked: it always takes its own room. Size sets how much it shows, from icons only to counts and details.
Stage shows the categories as a sheet that slides in with ◀, so the channel list and preview get the room. Separate keeps the categories on screen beside the list.
Cinematic shows the focused title’s artwork behind a grid of posters. Separate shows categories, titles and details side by side.
Pick which rows Home shows and in what order, and how the Now trending row looks.
Hide categories and items you never watch, give categories your own names and put them in your order. Hidden things come back here, never lost.
The OwnTV icon on your TV’s home screen. The launcher may take a moment to show the change.
The OwnTV logo in the menu, About and setup shows its play triangle in your accent color. The icon on the home screen keeps its own colors.
What OwnTV shows when it starts: Home, the channel you watched last, your favorites, or a channel you pick.
Looks on GitHub for a newer OwnTV now and offers to install it. Your playlists, favorites and settings stay as they are.
Looks for a new version each time OwnTV starts and tells you when there is one. Nothing is installed without asking.
Looks up your provider’s addresses with a DNS server of your choice instead of your network’s own — useful when your network blocks or redirects them.

ExoPlayer opens channels much faster and is the only one with live subtitles. mpv plays channels ExoPlayer can’t, including some unusual audio. The combined options try the other player when the first one fails.
Uses the TV’s hardware decoder: smooth 4K and less heat. Turn it off only if some streams stutter or show blocks; the software decoder then does the work.
The volume every channel, film and episode starts at. Above 100%% quiet streams are amplified. A volume you change in the player is kept for that title until you reset it.
Shows your provider’s channel number beside the name in the Live TV list, the channel-list overlay and the player, and lets you type a number on the remote in full screen to jump to that channel.
How far rewind and forward jump in a film or episode with one press. Holding the key keeps jumping.
How the picture fills the screen when playback starts. Fit shows the whole picture; the other choices fill, stretch or force a shape. A zoom changed in the player is kept for that title.
Subtitles in this language are switched on by themselves when a stream has them. Otherwise subtitles stay off until you pick a track in the player.
The focused channel plays in the preview beside the Live TV list, so you see what is on before you open it. Needs a layout with room for the preview.
Plays the preview’s sound as well as its picture. Off keeps browsing quiet.
How far back Pause and rewind live TV can go on a channel without catch-up. Longer keeps more of the channel in this device’s storage.
Ask to resume offers Resume or Start over when a film or episode has a saved position. Always resume carries on where you stopped; Never resume starts from the beginning.
The small player that keeps a channel going in a corner while you browse. Choose its size and the corner it sits in.
Changes show here as you move, before you leave the row.
